evals.prompt: Add a node that loads the trees.parquet and cta_stations.geojson files of the Chicago Loop Layers dataset and keeps the trees within 50 m of a CTA 'L' station.
evals.expected_output: One proposed Python node whose code loads each file on its own, curio_load_data("data.curio.chicago-loop-layers", part="trees.parquet") and curio_load_data("data.curio.chicago-loop-layers", part="cta_stations.geojson"), and returns the trees within 50 m of a station, opening no file by a path of its own.
assertions: The answer proposes one new node (node.create) of a Python code template, such as Python Computation, Data Transformation or Data Loading.
The proposed code loads the trees with curio_load_data("data.curio.chicago-loop-layers", part="trees.parquet"): the dataset's id and the file's name, each written as a string.
The code loads the stations the same way, with part="cta_stations.geojson".
The code opens no file by a path of its own: no gpd.read_file, pd.read_parquet or curio_data_path for either file.
The code returns the trees that lie within 50 m of a station.

evals.prompt: Add a node that reads only the cells of the SCOUT flood depth raster for 2050 to 2080 without NbS that lie inside this box: north 41.53, south 41.50, west -90.60, east -90.55. Return the mean depth of the cells that hold one.
evals.expected_output: One proposed Python node whose code reads the window with curio_load_data("data.scout.flood-depth-2050-2080-no-nbs", bounds=(-90.60, 41.50, -90.55, 41.53)), the box ordered west, south, east, north, and returns the mean of the cells that hold a depth.
assertions: The answer proposes one new node (node.create) of a Python code template.
The proposed code calls curio_load_data with the dataset id "data.scout.flood-depth-2050-2080-no-nbs" and a bounds argument.
The bounds are ordered west, south, east, north: (-90.60, 41.50, -90.55, 41.53), not in the order the prompt named them.
The code makes no window of its own: it opens no raster by a path (no rasterio.open on curio_data_path or a file name) and builds no rasterio window from the box.
The code reads the cells from the dataset curio_load_data returns, leaves out the cells with no value (masked or nodata), and returns their mean.

evals.prompt: In a Python node, label the Lincoln Park street photos with the street-scene segmentation model in my Model Catalog, and give me each photo's share of vegetation and of sky, with a link to its overlay.
evals.expected_output: One proposed Python node whose code reads the photos with curio_load_collection("data.curio.mapillary-sample"), loads the model with curio_load_model("model.curio.ddrnet23-slim"), and labels the photos with curio_segment(photos, model, classes=["vegetation", "sky"]), returning its rows with vegetation_pct, sky_pct and overlay_url.
assertions: The answer proposes one new node (node.create) of a Python code template.
The proposed code reads the photos with curio_load_collection("data.curio.mapillary-sample").
The code loads the model with curio_load_model and the model's id written as a string, model.curio.ddrnet23-slim (with or without @1).
The code labels the photos by calling curio_segment with the collection's rows and the loaded model, with classes naming vegetation and sky; it runs no model session and counts no pixels itself.
The code returns the rows curio_segment gives, or a part of them that keeps vegetation_pct, sky_pct and overlay_url.

evals.prompt: In a Python node, take one frame every half second from the video in the Example street survey collection, and return the frames as rows a Simple View can show as cards.
evals.expected_output: One proposed Python node whose code reads the collection with curio_load_collection("data.curio.storage-survey"), takes the video's row, and for each frame at 0, 500, 1000 ms and on gets where to write it from curio_derived_file(dataset_id, file_id, t_ms, kind="video"), writes the frame there, and returns the rows curio_derived_file gives.
assertions: The answer proposes one new node (node.create) of a Python code template.
The proposed code reads the collection with curio_load_collection("data.curio.storage-survey") and takes the video's row from it.
For each frame, the code calls curio_derived_file with the row's dataset_id and file_id, the frame's time in milliseconds (0, 500, 1000, ...) and kind="video".
The code writes each frame image to the path in the row curio_derived_file returns, and makes no folder or file path of its own (no tempfile, no hard-coded directory).
The code returns the frames' rows, which carry the thumbnail and image_url that curio_derived_file gives.
